questions.text: Why does Registry publication not by itself approve a server for production use?

options.A: Registry records cannot name versions or execution sources.
options.B: A live server’s display name is the only valid deployment authority.
options.C: Publication proves that the live toolset can never change.
options.D: Publication and local admission answer different questions; exact source and runtime evidence still need policy approval.

questions.explanation: Registry publication concerns declared metadata and naming authority. Local admission joins exact artifact/provenance and live descriptor evidence with deployment policy.

questions.text: An admitted version adds an unexpected destructive tool without changing its publication record. What does the lesson’s controller do?

options.A: Accept it because the Registry version and package identity are unchanged.
options.B: Update the descriptor pin automatically to preserve availability.
options.C: Quarantine and deactivate the pin, retaining evidence and blocking it as a rollback target.
options.D: Erase the admission history because the original observation is obsolete.

questions.explanation: The changed live toolset is runtime drift. The controller quarantines the pin, removes its active route, and preserves history rather than silently approving it.

questions.text: namespace_matches splits server_name at the first slash and requires a non-empty slug plus exact equality with verified_namespace. What does namespace_matches("com.exampleevil/inventory", "com.example") return?

options.A: True, because the server name starts with com.example.
options.B: False, because com.exampleevil does not exactly equal com.example.
options.C: True, because inventory is a non-empty slug.
options.D: It raises ValueError because the namespace has more than two components.

questions.explanation: The namespace prefix is compared for exact equality, preventing lookalike string-prefix acceptance.
